goals.name: Explore workspace and plan goal context

goals.description: Determine the service's supported webhook events, whether automatic webhook registration and deletion are available, expected payload shapes, and the repository's naming and implementation conventions for comparable triggers.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on research and inspection. Identify the concrete service name, trigger IDs, event names, event payload fields, whether a generic all-events webhook is appropriate, and whether the service API supports programmatic create/delete webhook endpoints. Inspect nearby trigger directories and block definitions for style, naming, icon imports, and registration patterns. Produce a concise implementation summary for successors; avoid modifying workspace files unless the user task explicitly requires recording research elsewhere.
goals.name: Research service webhook capabilities and existing conventions

goals.description: Derive the concrete checks that will verify the trigger implementation, including alignment checks, TypeScript checks, and any service-specific manual or automated validation expectations.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Prepare validation guidance from the researched service/event contract and existing repo scripts. Do not redesign implementation. Output a concrete validation plan for G007: acceptance criteria for trigger options, primary versus secondary dropdown behavior, registry and block wiring, optional automatic registration behavior, output/formatWebhookInput alignment, and exact commands such as `bunx scripts/check-trigger-alignment.ts <service>` and `bun run type-check` where applicable. If you create any helper validation script, write it only to an isolated non-owned path and record that path; otherwise keep this as a planning-only goal.
goals.name: Prepare validation acceptance criteria and commands

goals.description: Create or update the service trigger directory with utils, primary trigger, secondary triggers, optional generic webhook trigger, and barrel exports using the generic trigger builder.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Implement only the files under `apps/sim/triggers/<service>/` for the researched service. Create/update `utils.ts` with trigger options, setup instructions, extra fields, and outputs; create the primary trigger with `includeDropdown: true`; create secondary triggers without `includeDropdown`; create a generic all-events webhook trigger when appropriate; and update the local `index.ts` barrel exports. Use `buildTriggerSubBlocks` and ensure outputs follow trigger output schema rules. If automatic registration is supported, include the API key/password field and automatic setup instructions in the trigger UI helpers here.
goals.name: Create service trigger files

goals.description: Register the new triggers globally and connect them to the corresponding block's trigger configuration and trigger subBlocks.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Edit only the global trigger registry and the relevant service block file. Import the service triggers from the new barrel, add every trigger ID to `TRIGGER_REGISTRY`, enable triggers on `apps/sim/blocks/blocks/<service>.ts`, list all available trigger IDs, and spread every trigger's subBlocks via `getTrigger('<id>').subBlocks` after regular tool subBlocks. Preserve existing block behavior and ordering conventions.
goals.name: Wire triggers into registry and service block

goals.description: When the researched service supports programmatic webhook management, add provider-specific webhook creation after database save and non-fatal external cleanup on deletion.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Use the research result to decide whether automatic registration is supported. If not supported, leave backend files unchanged and report that manual setup remains required. If supported, edit `apps/sim/app/api/webhooks/route.ts` to create the external webhook after the database save, store the external webhook ID in `providerConfig.externalId`, return user-friendly errors, and roll back the database webhook on external creation failure. Also edit `apps/sim/lib/webhooks/provider-subscriptions.ts` to add a provider logger, a `delete<Service>Webhook` cleanup function, and a `cleanupExternalWebhook` branch that logs cleanup failures non-fatally. Keep providerConfig field names aligned with the trigger extra fields from G003.
goals.name: Implement automatic webhook registration and cleanup if supported

goals.description: Add or update provider-specific webhook payload formatting when needed so actual runtime data exactly matches the trigger output schema.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Compare the trigger outputs created in G003 with the researched webhook payloads and the existing generic fallback in `apps/sim/lib/webhooks/utils.server.ts`. If the raw payload already matches the outputs, do not add unnecessary formatting. If transformation is needed, add a provider handler that returns fields matching the trigger outputs exactly, with no wrapper objects or duplicate body spreading, and use null for missing optional data where appropriate. Keep this goal limited to webhook input formatting and related alignment fixes.
goals.name: Align webhook input formatting with trigger outputs

goals.description: Execute the prepared validation checks after all implementation work, fix any discovered issues, and summarize readiness and remaining manual testing needs.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Reuse the validation plan prepared in G002 rather than redesigning it, adapting only if actual workspace results require changes. Run the service-specific alignment checker, TypeScript check, and any prepared isolated validation scripts or relevant targeted checks. Inspect failures against the checklist: trigger files, dropdown behavior, registry entries, block wiring, optional automatic registration/cleanup, and output formatting alignment. Make focused repairs in the relevant implementation files, rerun failed checks when practical, and report final validation results plus any manual UI/dev-server testing still needed.
goals.name: Run final validation and repair issues
